walkthroughs.body_html:
Planetary Motion & Gravity — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Planetary Motion & Gravity brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Planetary Motion & Gravity.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who formulated the law of universal gravitation?
options: Kepler
Newton
Einstein
Galileo

mcqs.q: Planets sweep equal areas in equal times is which law?
options: First
Second
Third
Zeroth

mcqs.q: What is the cosmic microwave background?
options: Relic radiation from when the universe became transparent, about 380,000 years after the Big Bang.
Light from the most distant galaxies.
How far it can see.
Background noise from human microwave ovens.

mcqs.q: Why do astronomers infer the existence of dark matter?
options: Light from the most distant galaxies.
Because the universe looks dark at night.
Visible matter alone cannot account for galaxy rotation curves and gravitational lensing.
Dark matter has been directly observed in telescopes.

mcqs.q: What does a telescope's aperture primarily determine?
options: Light from the most distant galaxies.
Light-gathering ability and angular resolution.
Magnification.
How far it can see.
